title: Toy Model Superposition Under Correlated Inputs: Does Feature Correlation Change the Packing Geometry?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if correlation disrupts superposition geometry, SAE training may fail to disentangle correlated features even in principle, which is a fundamental limit on the SAE approach to interpretability. This directly informs whether the dominant interpretability paradigm can succeed.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: The modification is described as 'a few lines of code change to the data generator' of the existing canonical toy model codebase. The experiment is a parameter sweep over correlation strength. A beginner can modify the data generator and run the sweep with mentor guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: one parameter sweep (5 correlation values) on an existing, well-documented codebase. Single precise experiment with well-defined metrics (feature angles, effective stored features) and an obvious deliverable (comparison to uncorrelated baseline). Can go from start to result quickly.

novelty.reasoning: Anthropic's 'Toy Models of Superposition' (Elhage et al., 2022) already explores correlated and anti-correlated features, finding that correlated features tend toward orthogonal representations while anti-correlated features can share directions. The paper explicitly discusses how feature correlation affects superposition geometry. Additionally, 'Spectral Superposition: A Theory of Feature Geometry' (arXiv:2602.02224, Feb 2026) provides further theoretical treatment. The core question is partially addressed by the original paper's section on correlated features, though a more systematic parameter sweep over correlation strength could add incremental value.
